subtopic: Theorem of remote interior angles of a triangle
stem:
In figure 3.8, \(\angle ACD\) is an exterior angle of \(\triangle ABC\). \(\angle B = 40^\circ\), \(\angle A = 70^\circ\). Find the measure of \(\angle ACD\).

[In figure 3.8, \(\triangle ABC\) is drawn with the side BC produced beyond C up to the point D, so that \(\angle ACD\) is the exterior angle of the triangle at C. No measures are marked on the figure itself.]
diagramNote: Fig. 3.8 — triangle ABC with base BC produced beyond C to D; shows the exterior-angle configuration only, no measures marked on the figure.

stem: In \(\triangle PQR\), \(\angle P = 70^\circ\), \(\angle Q = 65^\circ\) then find \(\angle R\).

subtopic: Theorem of remote interior angles of a triangle
stem: The measures of angles of a triangle are \(x^\circ\), \((x-20)^\circ\), \((x-40)^\circ\). Find the measure of each angle.

subtopic: Theorem of remote interior angles of a triangle
stem: The measure of one of the angles of a triangle is twice the measure of its smallest angle and the measure of the other is thrice the measure of the smallest angle. Find the measures of the three angles.

subtopic: Theorem of remote interior angles of a triangle
stem:
In figure 3.9, measures of some angles are given. Using the measures find the values of \(x\), \(y\), \(z\).

[In figure 3.9 the points N, M, R lie on one straight line in that order and the ray runs on beyond R; the points T, E, M lie on a second straight line in that order and the ray runs on beyond T. The segments NE, EM and MN therefore form \(\triangle NEM\). The measures marked on the figure are \(\angle TEN = 100^\circ\) at E and \(\angle EMR = 140^\circ\) at M. The unknowns marked are \(x = \angle ENM\) at N, \(y = \angle NEM\) at E and \(z = \angle EMN\) at M.]
diagramNote: Fig. 3.9 — triangle NEM with side NM produced to R and side ME produced to T; carries the two given measures 100 degrees (angle TEN) and 140 degrees (angle EMR) and labels the three unknowns x, y, z.

subtopic: Theorem of remote interior angles of a triangle
stem:
In figure 3.10, line AB \(\parallel\) line DE. Find the measures of \(\angle DRE\) and \(\angle ARE\) using given measures of some angles.

[In figure 3.10 the ray AB starts at A and runs upward to the left. The points A, R, D lie on one straight line with R between A and D. The segments RE and DE are drawn and line DE runs on beyond E. The measures marked on the figure are \(\angle BAD = 70^\circ\) at A, between ray AB and ray AD, and \(\angle DER = 40^\circ\) at E, between ray ED and ray ER.]
diagramNote: Fig. 3.10 — zigzag B-A-R-D with A, R, D collinear, plus segment RE and line DE; carries the given measures 70 degrees (angle BAD) and 40 degrees (angle DER).

stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), bisectors of \(\angle A\) and \(\angle B\) intersect at point O. If \(\angle C = 70^\circ\). Find measure of \(\angle AOB\).

subtopic: Theorem of remote interior angles of a triangle
stem:
In Figure 3.11, line AB \(\parallel\) line CD and line PQ is the transversal. Ray PT and ray QT are bisectors of \(\angle BPQ\) and \(\angle PQD\) respectively.
Prove that \(m\angle PTQ = 90^\circ\).

[In figure 3.11 the points A, P, B lie on line AB with P between A and B, and the points C, Q, D lie on line CD with Q between C and D. The transversal PQ cuts line AB at P and line CD at Q, and the two bisectors ray PT and ray QT meet at the point T lying between the two parallel lines. No measures are marked on the figure.]
diagramNote: Fig. 3.11 — two parallel lines AB and CD cut by transversal PQ, with the bisectors PT of angle BPQ and QT of angle PQD meeting at T between the lines; configuration only, no measures marked.

subtopic: Theorem of remote interior angles of a triangle
stem:
Using the information in figure 3.12, find the measures of \(\angle a\), \(\angle b\) and \(\angle c\).

[In figure 3.12 a triangle is drawn with its base lying along a straight line that runs on beyond both base vertices, and each of the other two sides is also produced beyond the base vertex it meets. \(\angle a\) is the angle of the triangle at its top vertex. \(\angle b\) is the angle of the triangle at the left base vertex, and the angle vertically opposite to \(\angle b\) — the one between the leftward part of the base line and the downward extension of the left side — measures \(70^\circ\). \(\angle c\) is the angle of the triangle at the right base vertex, and the angle next to \(\angle c\) on the base line — the one between the rightward part of the base line and the side that rises to the top vertex — measures \(100^\circ\). The vertices of the triangle are not named in the figure.]
diagramNote: Fig. 3.12 — an unlabelled triangle whose base lies on a line produced both ways and whose two other sides are produced past the base; carries the given 70 degrees (vertically opposite to angle b) and 100 degrees (adjacent to angle c on the base line) and labels a, b, c.

subtopic: Theorem of remote interior angles of a triangle
stem:
In figure 3.13, line DE \(\parallel\) line GF ray EG and ray FG are bisectors of \(\angle DEF\) and \(\angle DFM\) respectively.
Prove that,
(i) \(\angle DEG = \frac{1}{2} \angle EDF\)
(ii) EF = FG.

[In figure 3.13 the points E, F, M lie on one straight line in that order and the ray runs on beyond M, so \(\angle DFM\) is the exterior angle of \(\triangle DEF\) at F. The bisector ray EG of \(\angle DEF\) and the bisector ray FG of \(\angle DFM\) meet at the point G. No measures are marked on the figure; the two equal halves of \(\angle DEF\) are shown by small circle marks at E and the two equal halves of \(\angle DFM\) by cross marks at F.]
diagramNote: Fig. 3.13 — triangle DEF with side EF produced beyond F to M, the bisector ray EG of angle DEF and the bisector ray FG of the exterior angle DFM meeting at G; equal halves shown by circle marks at E and cross marks at F, no measures given.
_note: Printed as one numbered question with two things to prove, (i) and (ii), from a single figure and setup — kept as ONE row per the band instruction. The printed stem runs 'line GF ray EG' with no punctuation between; transcribed as printed.
